chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Muḥammad ibn al-Nuʿmān, from Sallām, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, regarding His, the Exalted's, saying:
“Say: We believe in Allah and in what has been sent down to us.”
He said: “He only meant by that ʿAlī عليه السلام, and Fāṭimah, and al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḥusayn, and it continued after them among the Imams عليهم السلام.”
Then the address returns from Allah concerning the people, so He said:
“in the like of that which you believe in”
meaning ʿAlī, and Fāṭimah, and al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḥusayn, and the Imams عليهم السلام,
“then they have indeed been guided; and if they turn away, then they are only in dissension.”

key_terms.آمَنَّا: we believed; the declaration of faith and affirmation
key_terms.أُنْزِلَ: was sent down; referring to divine revelation
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةِ: the Imams عليهم السلام, continuing the same referent after the first four figures
key_terms.اهْتَدَوْا: they were rightly guided; attaining true guidance
key_terms.شِقَاقٍ: dissension; opposition and schism through turning away
key_terms.عَلِيًّا: ʿAlī عليه السلام, identified here as intended in the verse’s inner referent

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith interpret “Say: We believe in Allah” in relation to Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a tafsir of the Qur'anic declaration of faith by applying it specifically to ʿAlī عليه السلام, Fāṭimah, al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn, and the Imams عليهم السلام after them. It portrays guidance as being tied to belief in the wilayah and authority of Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام, while turning away from them is described as schism and opposition.
